# Summary of Studienstiftung
The Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes, initially founded in Dresden in 1925, was dissolved during National Socialism and reestablished in Cologne in 1948 as a registered association. It offers scholarships combining financial support and academic enrichment to exceptionally talented bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral students studying full-time at universities primarily in Germany, the EU, or Switzerland. Admission pathways include nominations by high schools, university professors, examination boards, national competition winners, and an assessment test, among others. The scholarship emphasizes "excellence, initiative, and responsibility," with financial aid amounting to up to €855 monthly (including allowances for health insurance and children), and for doctoral students, up to €1,550 monthly, plus research allowances. Academic support includes summer schools, workshops, mentoring, and funding for conferences organized by scholars themselves.
As of 2023, the Studienstiftung supports around 14,888 scholars (including 1,262 doctoral students), representing roughly 0.48% of students in Germany. It operates internal scholarship programs such as the KAUST-Studienstiftung and cooperates on open scholarship programs like the McCloy and ERP-Stipendienprogramm. Notable alumni span a wide range of fields including natural sciences, social sciences, politics, arts, journalism, and business, distinguished by numerous awards such as Nobel Prizes, Fields Medals, and Leibniz Prizes. Leadership history includes presidents like Adolf Grimme (1948–1963) and current president Michael Hoch (from 2023), as well as secretaries general such as Heinz Haerten (1948–1970) and Annette Julius (since 2012).
